basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 15.' and it opens 'VERS. 15.-- Hi filii Liae, quos genuit in Mesopotamia Syriae cum Dina; animae filiorum et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 15.-- Hi filii Liae, quos genuit in Mesopotamia Syriae cum Dina; animae filiorum et filiarum triginta tres. Nunquid istae omnes triginta et tres animae ex Lia in Mesopotamia Syriae natae sunt, dum ibi Jacob non plus viginti annis cum socero suo moratus est, et septem anni transierunt antequam Liam uxorem duxisset? Ideo etiam Scriptura sancta hos omnes in Mesopotamia ortos esse dixit, quoniam eorum patres ibi orti sunt.
